title: Region-aware ephemeral-lease + circuit-breaker for limiter outage recovery and fair burst absorption
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem statement: When our quota admission/limiter layer experiences transient partial outages (eg. redis lease store lag, regional control-plane partitions), customer-facing requests either get failed open (SLO regression) or get uniformly rejected (poor burst handling and unfairness). We need a resilient limiter behaviour that preserves tenant fairness, absorbs short bursts, and fails in a predictable, SLO-driven way across regions.

Goals:
- Maintain P99 latency and error SLOs for Hosted API customers during limiter partial failures where possible.
- Support short burst absorption without violating long-term quota guarantees.
- Ensure deterministic, auditable fallback behaviour during regional outages (circuit open, degraded admission).
- Preserve cross-tenant fairness (weighted by plan) and avoid noisy-neighbor starvation during emergency modes.

Non-goals:
- Re-architecting billing/usage accounting (we rely on eventual reconciliation for billing).
- Solving arbitrary global coordination under full control-plane outage (we assume at least eventual connectivity for reconciliation).

High-level approach:
1) Ephemeral-lease escrow: each region maintains a small, bounded lease reservoir per tenant that can be used to absorb bursts if the central quota store is unresponsive. Leases are time-limited and conservatively sized based on historical burst quantiles.
2) Region-aware circuit-breaker: a circuit state machine per region+tenant that moves to OPEN when the local quota store error rate or reconcile lag exceeds a threshold; in OPEN, admission falls back to a constrained local policy (lease-only + degraded fairness).
3) Soft load-shedding policy: implement progressive load-shedding hooks that drop low-priority or non-critical routes first, using token buckets and weighted fairness to keep high-priority traffic flowing.
4) Reconciliation and tombstones: after normal ops resume, a deterministic reconciliation process consumes escrowed leases against the authoritative store and emits audit events for billing/alerts.

Design details:
- Lease reservoir sizing: use 95th/99th burst quantiles by tenant class computed over a rolling 30d window. Reservoir capped by both absolute tokens and a percentage of tenant monthly commit to limit billing risk.
- Lease semantics: one-way, time-to-live (30s by default). Leases are redeemable only once and emit a redemption record to a local write-ahead log (WAL).
- Circuit thresholds: open if quota-store RPC error rate > 5% and median reconcile lag > 2s over a 1m window OR if WAL write latency exceeds 100ms p99. Close requires sustained health for 2m and grace token drain.
- Admission flow in OPEN: try local lease; if insufficient, attempt degraded admission with prioritized queues: SSO/authenticated admin, paid-plan API keys, free-tier. Within each priority, use weighted fair-queueing (weights derived from billing tier).
- Fairness: weights are normalized tokens-per-second; when region goes to OPEN, we compute temporary fairness windows to ensure high-weight tenants cannot grind the reservoir.
- Audit + billing: every lease redemption writes a WAL entry; reconciler batches WAL entries to the canonical usage store and marks reconciled tokens. Any redeemed-but-unreconciled tokens older than 1h create a reconciliation alert.

Telemetry & SLOs:
- Primary SLOs to protect: request_success_rate >= 99.5% at P99 for paid plans; p99 latency < 300ms for generation endpoints under normal load.
- New metrics to add: lease_issued_count, lease_redeemed_count, lease_reconcile_lag_seconds, region_circuit_state, escalated_shedding_rate_by_route, fairness_violation_ratio.
- Alerts: circuit_open_count > 0 for > 30s (pager), lease_reconcile_lag_seconds > 5m (oncall), fairness_violation_ratio > 0.1 for > 5m (ops slack).

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for lease allocator and conservative caps.
- Integration tests with local redis replica simulating latency spikes and failures.
- Chaos tests: inject packet loss / slow RPCs and assert circuit transitions and reconciliation occur.
- Load sims: replay production traffic slices with a spike template to verify fairness and SLOs under OPEN mode.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flagged rollout to internal sandbox tenants for 2 days.
2) Canary to 5% of production traffic in a single region for 48h with aggressive telemetry dashboards.
3) Gradual 25% -> 50% -> 100% regional rollouts across regions over 2 weeks, with rollback on any critical SLO violation.

Runbook (summary):
- If region circuit opens unexpectedly: check region_circuit_state dashboard, increase logging, and if OPEN persists > 5m escalate to infra. During OPEN, use quick knobs to tighten reservoir caps (reduce to 50%) to limit billing exposure.
- If reconciliation backlog grows: pause new lease issuance for affected tenants and trigger manual reconciliation job.

Open trade-offs and questions:
- Conservative vs aggressive reservoir sizing: conservative sizing reduces billing risk but may cause SLO regressions for bursty tenants. We propose tiered defaults with per-tenant override by ops.
- Consistency model: we accept eventual consistency and rely on WAL + reconciler; full global coordination is expensive and outside scope.
- Billing implications: redeemed leases are recorded and billed; we need legal/product alignment on how to communicate short-term emergency credits to customers.

Security & compliance note: lease WALs contain tenant IDs and token counts — ensure WAL encryption at rest and KMS access controls (we will reuse existing KMS paths used by usage service).
acceptance_criteria: Region-level circuit state machine implemented and unit-tested
Lease reservoir allocation and WAL write path verified with integration tests against a slow redis replica
Simulation shows P99 success_rate for paid plans not dropping below 99.5% under a modeled quota-store failure for 60s
Reconciler consumes WAL entries and marks tokens reconciled with < 5m average lag in canary
Dashboards and alerts created and validated in oncall runbook
Design doc and runbook reviewed and signed off by SRE, Billing, and Product
timeline: 2026-03-01: Ticket created after incident postmortem (INC-2026-02-28). Observed: transient redis latency causing >10s reconcile lag and customer-facing failures.
2026-03-03: Prototype lease allocator implemented and smoke tested against local harness (Aisha).
2026-03-05: Simulation results: 30s reservoir with 95th burst quantile improved P99 success_rate by 0.9% in the model.
2026-03-08: Architecture review with SRE and Billing; decision to use WAL + reconciler pattern and to cap per-tenant reservoir by both absolute and relative budgets (notes in design doc).
2026-03-10: Began implementation of circuit-state machine and added region_circuit_state metric (Marco).
decisions: Use ephemeral, time-limited leases rather than optimistic local counters to limit billing exposure
Adopt WAL+reconciler for eventual accounting guarantees
Circuit open criteria must combine RPC error rate and reconcile lag to avoid flapping on transient spikes
next_steps: Complete unit tests for WAL durability and p99 latency (owner: Marco)
Add canary simulation and fork Traffic Replay job for 5% canary (owner: Reliability)
Coordinate billing/product comms regarding emergency lease semantics and credits (owner: Product)
Schedule runbook tabletop with oncall and SRE (owner: SRE lead)
